title: Spec design: declarative membership keys for RLS (current_user.<key> from a lookup on records whose user field is the current user)
body:
Ruled: 6355640929 · letter A · 2026-10-23T02:04:08Z

Filing gate ②: from the maintainer's ruling on objectstack-ai/cloud#3149 (batch #386 item 5, item 2). Filed by `repo:cloud#1` (seat post #6026, session `session_01FSg7JRUiTPo8GrgT38tAWP`). ⛔ Not a claim. A **spec design card**: it adds protocol, ~~so the design is put to the maintainer before any implementation starts~~ (ruled A in 6355640929; implementation may be dispatched).

**Reader who acts:** the objectstack lane. objectstack-ai/cloud#3149 (the tracker) is `Blocked-by:` this card.

## The gap (cloud#3149 item 2)
- `rls-membership-resolver` (ADR-0105 D11) can express `supplier in current_user.portal_supplier_ids`, but only through code.
- Installed package code does not run on hosted (`docs/design/installed-package-handler-functions.md` in cloud).
- hotsrm (objectstack-ai/hotsrm#1) therefore uses one position per supplier, with RLS `portal_position in current_user.positions`. Every supplier-facing record must carry a stamped `portal_position`, and one missed stamp is an over-grant.

## The ask
- A declarative membership key in metadata, as the metadata twin of ADR-0105 D11: `current_user.<key>` = the values of lookup field F on records of object X whose user field U equals the current user.
- The design round names: the declaration's home (object or app), the closed shape (X, F, U, an optional filter), how it is cached per request, how a cycle or an unbounded set is refused at publish, and how it shows in the security explainers.

## Acceptance (for the design round)
A design comment the maintainer rules on, with the zod shape, the refusal list, one worked example (hotsrm's supplier contact), and the resolver path it reuses.
